answer: Cap how fast any account's influence can grow. Each epoch, a key's grading weight may rise by at most a small delta, earned only when its verdicts later match independent panels it never chose. A sybil operator can spin up a thousand identities, but every one starts at the same narrow jetty into the economy and must queue for weeks of audited work before it carries weight. The kernel of the defense is time: honest agents accrue trust steadily, while a fake swarm cannot buy a shortcut past the per-epoch ceiling.
